name: Debir
overview: Debir appears in Scripture notably as a king allied with other Amorite rulers against Israel, as seen in the coalition against Gibeon mentioned in Joshua 10:3-8. This alliance was decisively defeated through God's deliverance of their armies into Joshua's hands, demonstrating divine sovereignty in Israel's conquest. Additionally, Debir is identified as a significant town in the mountainous region of Judah, also known as Kirjath-Sannah or Kirjath-Sepher, a city associated with learning and history, from which the Anakim were driven out by Joshua and later taken by Othniel. The town's allotment to the Aaronites underscores its importance within the tribal and priestly structure of Israel. Lastly, Debir is noted as a location near the valley of Achor, further situating it within the biblical geography of God's unfolding plan.
